title: Airbnb cleaning checklist: a printable room-by-room turnover list
summary: A printable, room-by-room Airbnb turnover cleaning checklist: kitchen, bedrooms, bathrooms, outdoor areas, restocking and photos.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**A good turnover checklist is short enough to finish and specific enough to check. Below is a room-by-room Airbnb cleaning checklist you can copy, print or paste into any app: 56 items across eight sections, ordered the way a clean actually runs, with the photo shots at the end. It's built for a clean that takes about two hours, which is the median turnover in our data.**


## Key takeaways


- **Order matters more than length.** Strip beds and start laundry first, floors last, photos at the very end.
- **The median turnover clean takes about two hours** in our data: about 85 minutes for a studio or one-bedroom and about 200 for five bedrooms or more ([full benchmarks](https://prohost.ai/blog/turnover-cleaning-time-benchmarks) ).
- **Check what guests check.** Value, accuracy and cleanliness are the lowest sub-scores on 1 to 3 star reviews, so the last pass is about what a guest sees in the first five minutes.
- **Put the checklist where the cleaner works.** A paper list on the counter works. A list on the cleaner's phone, in their language, with photos attached, works better.
- **Prune it every quarter.** A checklist that grows without pruning stops being read.

## Where we're coming from


I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team, and we host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree, where we hold a[4.99 rating across thousands of guest stays](https://prohost.ai/about) . Cleanliness is where reviews are won and lost: across 135,352 reviews on ProhostAI in the last year, the cleanliness sub-score on 1 to 3 star reviews averaged **3.0 out of 5** , against **4.92** on 5-star reviews. This checklist is what a clean needs to cover so that gap never opens.


## The room-by-room turnover checklist (copy this)


Fill in the blanks for each property: where linens are kept, the lockbox code for supplies, the trash day.


### 1. Arrival (5 minutes)


- Tap start (or note the time).
- Walk every room before touching anything. Photograph any damage, missing items or anything left behind.
- Open windows if the weather allows.
- Strip every bed, collect towels, start the first laundry load.
- Empty every trash can and recycling bin.


### 2. Kitchen


- Run, empty and wipe the dishwasher. Put away clean dishes.
- Wash anything left in the sink. Check cabinets for dirty dishes.
- Clean the inside of the microwave.
- Wipe stovetop, oven front, range hood and knobs.
- Empty the fridge of guest food. Wipe shelves and door seals.
- Empty the coffee maker, rinse the carafe, clear the grounds.
- Wipe counters, backsplash, cabinet fronts and handles.
- Clean the sink and faucet. Run the disposal.
- Restock: dish soap, sponge, dishwasher tabs, paper towels, coffee, filters, salt, pepper, oil.
- Check that pots, pans, knives and utensils match the inventory.


### 3. Living and dining areas


- Dust surfaces, shelves, TV stand and picture frames.
- Wipe the TV screen, remotes, light switches and door handles.
- Fluff and arrange cushions. Fold throws.
- Vacuum sofa cushions and under them.
- Wipe the dining table and chairs.
- Check that the TV, streaming apps and Wi-Fi work. Sign out of any guest accounts.
- Reset thermostat and blinds to your standard.


### 4. Bedrooms


- Make every bed with fresh linens, the same way every time.
- Check mattress protectors and pillows for stains.
- Look under beds and in drawers and closets for left items.
- Dust nightstands, lamps and headboards.
- Check hangers, the luggage rack, extra blankets and pillows.
- Test every lamp and the bedside chargers.


### 5. Bathrooms


- Clean and disinfect the toilet: bowl, seat, base and behind it.
- Scrub the shower or tub, walls, glass and fixtures. Clear the drain.
- Clean the sink, faucet, counter and mirror.
- Wipe cabinet fronts and handles.
- Hang fresh towels and a bath mat, folded the same way every time.
- Restock: toilet paper (at least two spare rolls), soap, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, tissues.
- Empty the trash and replace the liner.
- Flush every toilet and run every faucet to check for leaks and hot water.


### 6. Outdoor areas


- Sweep the entry, porch, deck or balcony.
- Wipe outdoor furniture and arrange it.
- Clean and empty the grill. Check the propane level.
- Check the hot tub or pool: cover on, water clear, chemistry logged.
- Take trash and recycling to the bins. Note the next pickup day: ___.
- Check exterior lights and the door code keypad.


### 7. Floors and final touches


- Vacuum every room, including corners and under furniture.
- Mop hard floors, starting at the farthest room and working toward the door.
- Fold and put away clean linens and towels. Note any that are stained or worn.
- Set out welcome items and the house manual.
- Close windows. Set the thermostat to the arrival setting.
- Note supplies running low: ___.
- Note anything broken, loose or not working: ___.


### 8. Photos and finish


- Photo of each bedroom with the bed made.
- Photo of each bathroom.
- Photo of the kitchen counters and sink.
- Photo of the living area.
- Photo of anything damaged or left behind, with a note.
- Lock up. Test the door code from outside.
- Tap complete (or note the time).


## How to make the checklist stick


- **Laminate one copy per property** and keep it in the cleaning closet, or better, put it on the cleaner's phone.
- **Give it to cleaners in their language.** A checklist a cleaner reads quickly is a checklist that gets done.
- **Ask for photos, not ticks.** A photo of a made bed proves more than a checked box.
- **After a bad review, add one line,** not five. After three months, remove the lines nobody has needed.
- **Time the cleans.** If one property runs long every time, the checklist (or the property) needs a look.

## FAQ


### What should be on an Airbnb cleaning checklist?


Every room the guest uses, in the order the clean runs: arrival walk-through and laundry, kitchen, living areas, bedrooms, bathrooms, outdoor areas, floors, then photos. Include restocking lists and a place to note damage and low supplies.


### How long does it take to clean an Airbnb?


In our data the median turnover clean took about two hours: about 85 minutes for a studio or one-bedroom and about 200 minutes for five bedrooms or more.


### Should cleaners take photos?


Yes. Photos of each room on finish give you proof the clean happened, a record if a guest complains, and a way to check new cleaners without visiting.


### How often should I update my checklist?


Review it every quarter. Add a line when a guest complaint shows a gap, and remove lines that never catch anything.


## The takeaway


Copy the list, cut what doesn't apply, fill in the blanks for each home, and put it where the cleaner works, in their language. Then check the photos.
